messages:
anya: Heads up — apiserver is returning 503s in eu-central1 since ~08:15 UTC, controller-manager is lagging. Not seeing obvious deploys.

sam: Yep, seeing a sharp p95 spike on k8s_apiserver_request_latency. etcd follower timeouts in the logs around the same window.

ops-bot: alert: apiserver_eu-central1_503_rate > threshold at 2026-03-18T08:15:12Z :pagerduty: <https://pagerduty.example/incident/1234>

mike: Quick inventory:
```
$ kubectl -n kube-system get pods
kube-apiserver-eu-0   Running   3   5m
kube-apiserver-eu-1   Running   0   2d
kube-controller-manager-1   CrashLoopBackOff   4   10m
```
kube-controller-manager logs show repeated 'binding queue processing slow' and OOM-ish restarts. etcd logs: "wal: sync timed out" and "rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded".

lucy: Checking infra metrics — etcd EBS iops spiked at 08:09–08:17 (sustained). I also see a scheduled compaction job that kicked at 08:09 on the leader. Disk wait climbed.

dinesh: Confirmed: compaction cron ran on the leader at 08:09. Snapshot + WAL GC created a burst of disk writes. At the same time, we have a lot of GPU attach/detach activity from recent ML batch jobs — kubelet attach retries are frequent.

anya: Could the GPU attach/detach churn be amplifying kubelet and controller-manager load (lots of attach detach events -> binding/volume controller pressure -> apiserver fanout)? Any fd/ephemeral metrics?

sam: Kubelet logs on noisy nodes show attach timeout loops from nvidia-device-plugin and kubelet issuing repeated attach calls. controller-manager binding queue length increased by ~6x. controller-manager CPU saturating ~95% on leader.

mike: Short-term mitigation options: cordon the noisy GPU nodes, scale down non-critical GPU pools, and postpone the etcd compaction if safe. Defrag/compaction during high traffic is risky.

lucy: We can also throttle the ML autoscaler (cap burst) so fewer concurrent attach operations. I'll prepare a temporary limit.

dinesh: For context: moving to Dedicated reserved GPUs would eliminate attach churn (static infra) but costs more. Not for now — prefer operational knobs.

anya: @sam can you run etcdctl member status + defrag on leader? Want to see member health and whether a defrag helps follower timeouts.

sam: ran quick checks:
```
etcdctl --endpoints=https://10.0.1.11:2379 endpoint status
member 1 (leader): healthy
member 2: unhealthy (timeout)
member 3: healthy
```
Defrag attempted but it was slow — defrag RPCs hit high disk latency. Follower eventually returned as disk io subsided.

oncall-uk: I'm taking oncall. Rolling leader isn't great since election causes more apiserver churn, but if leader disk is the problem we might need to move it. Will coordinate.

dinesh: operational note: if we keep hitting this pattern, we should evaluate moving compaction to off-peak and consider larger EBS volume IOPS for etcd or switching to faster disk tier. Also revisit autoscaler policies to avoid large burst spikes.

anya: Agreed. Proposed immediate runbook: 1) cordon 3 highest-churn GPU nodes 2) scale down autoscaler burst to 20% (temporary) 3) postpone scheduled compactions until maintenance window 4) restart controller-manager on leader if backlog doesn't drain 5) monitor apiserver p95/p99 and etcd member health.

lucy: I've applied a temp patch to cluster-autoscaler caps — PR: <https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/482> (will revert after stability).

ops-bot: incident: mitigation actions executed by anya at 3317778890

sam: Update: apiserver latency back down to baseline, 503s dropped to near zero after cordons + autoscaler cap. Unhealthy follower rejoined after disk pressure reduced and we completed defrag during low traffic.

anya: We'll keep the cordons for 30m and then slowly uncordon nodes one at a time while watching apiserver. If it recurs, open a postmortem and consider increasing etcd disk tier or changing compaction schedule.

anya: Closing provisional incident after 1h if stable. Please file follow-up if you see similar spikes in next 7 days — we should track recurrence. :white_check_mark:
